([[Exeter, New Hampshire]]) | college = * [[Williams Ephs men's basketball|Williams]] (2013–2014) * [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]] (2015–2018) | draft_year = 2018 | career_start = 2018 | years1 = {{nbay|2018|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Miami Heat]] | years2 = [[2018–19 NBA G League season|2018–2019]] | team2 = →[[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team3 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|NBA G League All-Rookie Team]] ([[2018–19 NBA G League season|2019]]) * Third-team All-NBA G League (2019) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Sixth Man of the Year (2018) * [[NCAA Division III|Division III]] Rookie of the Year (2014) * Fourth-team Division III [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] (2014) * Second-team All-[[New England Small College Athletic Conference|NESCAC]] (2014) }} '''Duncan McBryde Robinson''' (born April 22, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Detroit Pistons]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[NCAA Division III]] [[Williams Ephs|Williams College Ephs]] and then the [[NCAA Division I]] [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. He transferred to Michigan after leading Williams College to the [[2014 NCAA Division III men's basketball tournament]] championship game. At Michigan, he was part of the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 team]] that lost to [[2017–18 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the [[2018 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Championship Game|championship game]] of the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]]. Robinson led the [[Big Ten Conference]] in three-point shooting percentage (.450) from the beginning of conference play in December 2015 until early February 2016. In his three-year career at Michigan, he was a member of conference tournament champions in [[2017 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2017]] and [[2018 Big Ten Conference men's basketball tournament|2018]]. Robinson was the 2018 Big Ten Conference Sixth Man of the Year. After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], he signed with the [[Miami Heat]]. Robinson set numerous three-point shot records during his tenure with the Heat and helped Miami reach the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2020 NBA Finals|2020]] and [[2023 NBA Finals|2023]]. He is the only player from Williams College to ever play in the NBA. ==Early life== Born April 22, 1994, in [[York, Maine]], Robinson is the son of Elisabeth and Jeffrey Robinson and the youngest of their three children (after sister Marta and brother Eli). He is part [[Native Hawaiians|Hawaiian]] on his mother's side.{{cite web |title=Things You May Not Know: Feat. Duncan Robinson |url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/things-you-may-not-know-feat-duncan-robinson-02012022 |website=NBA.com |access-date=4 February 2022 |date=1 February 2022 |archive-date=February 4, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204124821/https://www.nba.com/heat/news/things-you-may-not-know-feat-duncan-robinson-02012022 |url-status=live }} Robinson grew up in the town of [[New Castle, New Hampshire]] (population 1,000), where his Maude H. Trefethen Elementary School 6th grade graduating class was composed of just four students.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/08/duncan_robinson.html|title=For Michigan's Duncan Robinson, the long wait for a long-shot D-III to D-I story is almost over|access-date=December 9, 2015|date=August 5, 2015|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.|archive-date=December 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210214203/http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/08/duncan_robinson.html|url-status=live}} == High school career == Robinson attended Rye Junior High School and elected to attend [[The Governor's Academy]] in Massachusetts rather than [[Portsmouth High School (New Hampshire)|Portsmouth High School]], which is the public high school for students in New Castle.{{cite web|author=Leveille|first=Jeremy|date=October 4, 2012|title=Robinson Commits to Williams|url=http://www.nhnotebook.com/2012/10/robinson-commits-to-williams.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210181909/http://www.nhnotebook.com/2012/10/robinson-commits-to-williams.html|archive-date=December 10, 2015|access-date=December 8, 2015|publisher=NHNotebook.com}} Robinson began his freshman season as a {{convert|5|ft|7|in|m|2|adj=on}} [[point guard]] for The Governor's Academy in 2008, but did not play much until he became "serviceable" as a junior. In his early years, he practiced shooting for hours, attempting to make 1,600 shots per week. Robinson started working with trainer Noah LaRoche during his junior season. After averaging 18.5 [[point (basketball)|points]] as a senior at The Governor's Academy, he was selected to the 2012 All-[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council|NEPSAC]] Class B first team and the 2012 All-[[Independent School League (Boston area)|Independent School League]] (ISL) team.{{cite web|url=http://www.nepsac.org/page/3086/article/748|title=2011 – 2012 NEPSAC Boys' Basketball All-New England Selections|access-date=December 8, 2015|publisher=[[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council]]|archive-date=December 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210212514/http://www.nepsac.org/page/3086/article/748|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2012/03/31/preps-all-scholastics/M3sTirIQ1DoQxtIH4SjZzN/story.html|title=2012 Preps All-Scholastics|access-date=December 8, 2015|date=April 1, 2012|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|author=Torres, Liz|archive-date=February 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190216094156/https://www.bostonglobe.com/sports/2012/03/31/preps-all-scholastics/M3sTirIQ1DoQxtIH4SjZzN/story.html|url-status=live}} He graduated with a 3.55 [[G.P.A.]] Following his senior season, Robinson played on the spring and summer [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit and did a [[postgraduate year]] at [[Phillips Exeter Academy]] in order to increase his college prospects. He led Exeter to a 28–1 record, ending on an 18-game win streak that included the [[NEPSAC]] Class A title. Robinson posted 24 points and 10 rebounds in the championship game, earning the Tournament MVP in addition to 2013 New England Preparatory School Athletic Council (NEPSAC) Class A All-League first team honors.{{cite web|url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/r/robinson-duncan.aspx|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706115558/https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/r/robinson-duncan.aspx|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 6, 2022|title=Duncan Robinson|accessdate=May 25, 2023|date=June 2, 2021|publisher=[[USA Basketball]]}} Robinson played for Michael Crotty Jr.'s Middlesex Magic AAU team. Crotty had been a two-time All-American at [[Williams College]],{{cite web|url=http://ephsports.williams.edu/sports/mbkb/History/All-Americans|title=All-Americans Since 1971|access-date=December 9, 2015|publisher=[[Williams College]]|archive-date=December 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210214435/http://ephsports.williams.edu/sports/mbkb/History/All-Americans|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.d3hoops.com/awards/all-americans/men/alltime|title=All-time D3hoops.com men's All-Americans|access-date=December 9, 2015|publisher=D3Hoops.com}} having served as point guard for the 2003 NCAA Division III Tournament champions (and 2004 Tournament runners up). Following his senior season, Robinson measured {{convert|6|ft|6|in|m|2}} and {{convert|175|lbs|kg|1}}. By the end of the summer, he had grown to {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|2}} and {{convert|195|lbs|kg|1}}. During the last weekend of September 2012 while on a campus visit, Division III Williams made Robinson an offer that he accepted immediately. At the time, Williams was ranked the number one liberal arts college in the country according to ''[[U.S. News & World Report]]'', and the school was a Division III basketball powerhouse. They had gone 93–22 over the prior four seasons under [[head coach]] [[Mike Maker (basketball)|Mike Maker]]. In 2013, Robinson led Phillips Exeter Academy to its first NEPSAC Class A championship victory on March 10 against [[Choate Rosemary Hall]] with a 24-point, 10-[[rebound (basketball)|rebound]] MVP performance.{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/regionals/north/2013/03/10/phillips-exeter-basketball-crowning-moment-class/tTsjMNGCZokn7Hcgh16tuL/story.html|title=Plots aplenty as teams wrap up season|access-date=December 8, 2015|date=March 10, 2013|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|author=Bradley, Pat|archive-date=December 10, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210212250/https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/regionals/north/2013/03/10/phillips-exeter-basketball-crowning-moment-class/tTsjMNGCZokn7Hcgh16tuL/story.html|url-status=live}} Exeter finished the season at 28–1. Nonetheless, his only scholarship offer was from [[NCAA Division II]]'s [[Merrimack College]]. He also had interest from Division I [[Brown Bears men's basketball|Brown Bears]] and [[Columbia Lions men's basketball|Columbia Lions]] as well as Division III [[Bates College]] and [[Amherst College]].{{cite web|url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2014/03/division-3-final-four-ncaa-basketball-salem-wisconsin-whitewater-williams|title=The best NCAA tournament game this weekend wasn't on your bracket: For The Win traveled to Salem, Virginia for the Division III men's national championship|access-date=December 9, 2015|date=March 24, 2014|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Strauss, Chris}} ==College career== ===Williams College=== Prior to the November 15, 2013, season opener against [[Southern Vermont College]], Williams was ranked third among Division III teams according to the preseason poll. Williams lost in the shadow of a home court scheduling conflict despite 5–6 shooting by Robinson. Robinson became the only freshman starter in Maker's six-year tenure as head coach at Williams. In his 2013–14 freshman season at Williams, Robinson was twice named [[New England Small College Athletic Conference]] (NESCAC) Player of the Week during the regular season.{{cite web|url=https://nescac.com/news/2000/1/1/1_1_2000_1786.aspx|title=2013–14 Men's Basketball Players of the Week|access-date=May 8, 2022|date=December 2, 2013|publisher=[[New England Small College Athletic Conference]]|archive-date=May 8, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220508140303/https://nescac.com/news/2000/1/1/1_1_2000_1786.aspx|url-status=live}} Williams reached the [[2014 NCAA Men's Division III basketball tournament]] championship game, but fell 75–73 to [[University of Wisconsin–Whitewater]] as Robinson scored 17 points.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2014-03-22/wisconsin-whitewater-edges-williams-win-diii-national|title=Wis.-Whitewater edges Williams to win DIII title|access-date=May 8, 2022|date=March 22, 2014|publisher=[[NCAA.org]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|author=Kurz Jr., Hank|archive-date=August 9, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809170803/https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2014-03-22/wisconsin-whitewater-edges-williams-win-diii-national|url-status=live}} After Williams took a one-point lead with 4.9 seconds left, Wisconsin pushed the ball upcourt without calling [[time-out (sports)|time-out]] to score the winning basket in what Chris Strauss of ''[[USA Today]]'' described as the best NCAA basketball tournament game of the weekend. Robinson had posted 30 points in the tournament semifinals against bitter rival [[Amherst College]] who had defeated Williams in the season's three previous meetings. Robinson had played against [[Nik Stauskas]] in NEPSAC play and was impressed with how Michigan's [[John Beilein]] had developed "under-recruited players" such as Stauskas who was a 1st round selection in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. Maker had been an assistant coach for Beilein at [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] from 2005 to 2007. At both Exeter and Williams, Robinson had played in systems that were similar to the one that Beilein runs at Michigan. Robinson asked Maker to contact Beilein who on faith replied that Michigan may have interest at the preferred [[Walk-on (sports)|walk-on]] level. Robinson was not interested in walk-on consideration given competing scholarship offers. A week later, after seeing video, Beilein said Michigan was considering a scholarship offer. Robinson scheduled visits to Michigan and new Atlantic 10 member [[Davidson Wildcats men's basketball|Davidson]]. After the visit to Michigan, Robinson committed to the school.
